title: Donating blood
what: You donate about 450 mL (about 1 pint) of blood, or a part of it, such as plasma or platelets, for free. This blood saves other people's lives.
why: Donor blood is needed for surgery, injuries, childbirth, and treatment of cancer and blood disorders.
duration: usually about an hour with the form and checkup; giving whole blood takes about 10 minutes, plasma takes longer
tell_doctor: All your illnesses and medicines. Answer the form honestly
Recent tattoos, piercings, surgery, or travel
If you were recently ill or took antibiotics
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding

prepare.title: Requirements
prepare.text: Usually a donor can be a healthy adult aged 18 or older, weighing at least 50 kg (110 lb). The blood center will tell you the exact rules.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not come hungry. Have a light, low-fat breakfast: porridge made with water, crackers, sweet tea.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: No alcohol for 2 days before. The day before, no fatty food, and get a good sleep. Do not smoke for an hour before donating.

steps: You fill out a health form
A drop of blood from your finger is tested for hemoglobin
A doctor checks your blood pressure and does a short exam
You lie down in the donor chair
A needle goes into a vein in the bend of your elbow, and blood collects in a bag
The needle comes out, and a bandage is put on
feel: A prick when the needle goes in
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse right away
after: Sit for 10 to 15 minutes and drink sweet tea
Keep the bandage on for 3 to 4 hours
That day, drink more, and avoid heavy exercise and alcohol
You can donate again only after the time the blood center tells you
red_flags: Fainting again or strong weakness at home: tell a doctor
Your arm becomes swollen, very painful, or numb

faq.q: Can I catch an infection by donating blood?
faq.a: No. Needles and bags are single-use and opened in front of you.

faq.q: How long does it take to recover?
faq.a: The fluid comes back in 1 to 2 days. Blood cells take a few weeks, so a break is needed between donations.

reminders.text: Blood donation tomorrow. Today, no fatty food or alcohol, and get a good sleep. Have a light breakfast. Do not come hungry.
